questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The available courses and the culture of the country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was made relatively easy as I stayed in a student accommodation with other international students in the same situation as myself and with other native students who were able to guide. If I had to find all the necessary information about living in Milan and going to UniMi im assuming it would have been a great deal more difficult to figure everything out. That said, the contact with the Erasmus coordinator was very effective, and I had that contact for great guidance as well.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received information about practical matters for school through the professors at the university. For the rest of the practical information I relied on other international students and the Erasmus team.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I always had the opportunity to ask the Erasmus counselor, which was a nice safety net, but it could have been communicated better, that they could help with a very wide range of practical questions.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: As far as I understood, there were two different student campuses. The one I stayed in had shared rooms with one other person available.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: A shared kitchen and a cafe.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I think the website of the campus presented the most necessary information.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Had to search for the classes in the student portal and assign yourself to them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A thorough guide.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I didn't have problems registering for classes, and if I had difficulties, there was a guide.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use the guides available on the website rather than waiting for an e-mail reply from the institution.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had masters levels courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It is more interactive at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Introduction to R, Advertising communication, Economics of Communication and Behavioral Sociology.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Behavioral Sociology. The professor is obviously interested in what he is teaching, which shows and makes him more interesting to listen to. Furthermore it is the most varied of the classes I took.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Fitness/gym was double the amount of the average in Denmark. Long haul train tickets and public transportation in general was much cheaper, which made it very easy to explore the country via train.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't attend any.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was many social clubs, and the ones I encountered was mostly about politics/student rights.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: In the city I would recommend areas such as Brera or Porta Venezia for the atmosphere, both by day and night. For exchange students staying in Milan I would recommend taking the train to cities such as Bergamo, Verona and Genova for one day trips.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The language barrier, but it wasn't really that big of a problem.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness of the people I met. It was very easy getting to know new people and making friends.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- A lot of the practical stuff will not be completely done by the time of arrival, but can be done upon/after arrival.
- Get to know natives from the courses, they can be very helpful with the practical understanding of the school system/exams etc.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The social part was very rewarding.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was navigating a new school system, where the employees of the institution that I encountered mostly spoke Italian.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
